name: 蒙古牛肉 (Ménggǔ Niúròu) · Mongolian Beef
description: The Chinese-American takeout classic (which has nothing to do with Mongolia): velveted flank steak fried crisp in cornstarch, tossed in a glossy soy and brown sugar glaze with scallions and dried chilies. Serves 4.

ingredients.text: 450 g flank steak, sliced against the grain 6 mm thick
ingredients.item: flank steak, sliced against the grain 6 mm thick

ingredients.text: 2 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
5 scallions, cut into 5 cm lengths, whites and greens apart
ingredients.item: scallions, cut into 5 cm lengths, whites and greens apart

steps.text: Toss 450 g flank steak, sliced against the grain 6 mm thick with 1/4 tsp baking soda and 1 tbsp water (for the marinade), then 1 tsp cornstarch (for the marinade) and 1 tsp neutral oil (for the marinade). Marinate 30 minutes.
Stir together 60 ml soy sauce, 1 tsp dark soy sauce, 50 g brown sugar and 120 ml hot water until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the beef in 40 g cornstarch (for dredging) until every slice is coated, shaking off excess.

Heat 160 ml neutral oil (for frying) in a wok over high until just shy of smoking. Spread the beef out in a single layer (in 2 batches if needed) and fry 1 minute per side, until crisp. Transfer to a plate and pour off all but 1 tbsp oil.

Over medium heat, fry 1 tsp ginger, minced and 6 dried red chilies for 15 seconds, add 4 garlic cloves, minced and the scallion whites from 5 scallions, cut into 5 cm lengths, whites and greens apart and stir 15 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 2 minutes, then stir in 2 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water and cook until it coats a spoon, about 30 seconds.
Return the beef with the scallion greens and toss 30 seconds, just to glaze. Serve right away with rice.

notes: The baking soda velveting is what makes flank steak tender at this thickness; don't skip the 30 minutes. Fry hot and fast and toss briefly at the end so the coating stays crisp under the glaze. The sauce is meant to be sweet; drop the sugar to 35 g if you prefer it more savory.
